messages:
sara_ml: Heads-up — nightly multilingual eval (03/18 -> 03/19) shows a spike in plausibility failures for JA/ZH -> EN translation. +7.8% adequacy drop on nightly set compared to yesterday. samples attached below.

kai_chang: ugh, saw that alert too. is this correlated with the tokenizer change from yesterday? we rolled a new BPE merge list at 03:00 UTC.

mohit_r: I pushed an experimental int8 quantization kernel around the same time (commit a9b3f2). Could be either tokenization or quant side-effect. bisect will tell.

sara_ml: sample from eval: 
```
SRC (ja): 彼は午後に来る予定です。
REF (en): He is expected to arrive in the afternoon.
OUT (en) : He will be coming in the afternoon, I think.
FILTER: plausibility_low (0.22)
```
not catastrophic but many outputs are adding hedging or hallucinated timeframe shifts.

eva_z: I pulled the nightly logs and reran a minimal eval locally with the same model snapshot. command I used: `python tools/eval_translation.py --suite nightly_multilang --langs ja,zh --model rwd-v2-2026-03-18 --seed 42 --batch 8`

eva_z: local run reproduces the increased hedging tokens for ja->en samples. switching to previous tokenizer revision (before BPE change) fixes the majority of those cases.

kai_chang: great narrowing. can you paste the tokenizer commit hash you tested?

eva_z: tested with tokenizers@f3c11dd (old) vs tokenizers@5a2b9e1 (new). old -> adequacy +6.1% relative.

mohit_r: quick note: the int8 kernel also changed how we handle BOS/EOS trimming for some ops. I can revert the trimming patch on a branch to test interaction.

sara_ml: can we do a 2D test matrix: (old/new tokenizer) x (old/new quant/kernel)? that will tell us whether it's purely tokenizer or an interaction. jenny_pm can we prioritize this for rollback window?

jenny_pm: We can hold the BPE roll for a hotfix if evidence points there. what's the customer impact? any high-traffic tenants affected?

sara_ml: early look: affects ja/zh -> english only on small-context samples; hit on nightly eval set primarily. no customer escalations yet, but quality regressions can cascade to downstream rerankers. want to be conservative.

mohit_r: I'll run the 2x2 matrix on a small shard now. command: `./ci/run_matrix.sh --tests ja,zh --snapshots old_tok,new_tok --kernels old_q,new_q`

ci-bot: job started: run/eng-ml/matrix/1802500487 (ETA ~12m). logs: https://ci.internal/runs/1802500487

eva_z: interim results from first shard: new_tok + old_q -> regression present. old_tok + new_q -> small regression but much smaller. new_tok + new_q -> worst. suggests tokenizer is the primary driver, quant amplifies it.

kai_chang: that pattern points at tokenization splitting producing extra subtokens around polite particles in JA and causing alignment shift, which leads to high-prob hedging tokens.

mohit_r: opened PR restoring previous BPE merge list and adding a compatibility test: https://git.internal/r/pr/4185 — also adding a regression test case from the failing sample.

sara_ml: thanks. let's coordinate: if CI confirms fix (+restore) improves nightly metrics we schedule a revert of the tokenizer change and keep quant kernel as-is for now.

jenny_pm: I'll notify releases and patch window team. planning 1h rollback window tomorrow 03/20 02:00 UTC if metrics look good. @sara_ml can you prepare the eval diff for release notes?

sara_ml: will export the before/after metric table and 20 representative examples. putting them in the incident folder.

kai_chang: follow-up item — add an automated tokenization-sensitivity test for multilingual evals so future BPE merges run a quick adequacy check on a small seed set.

eva_z: +1. added a TODO in repo: tools/eval_translation.py -> add `--tokenizer-sanity` mode.

mohit_r: I'll also add a unit test asserting BOS/EOS handling unchanged by quant kernels.

sara_ml: great. thanks everyone. we'll reconvene after CI finishes and before rollback decision. :thumbsup:
